narrationScript: Welcome to Chapter 5.4, where we'll dive into the crucial world of designing relational databases, focusing on normalization and SQL joins. In previous chapters, you learned the basics of SQL commands like SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE. Now, we'll explore how to structure your database tables efficiently to avoid common pitfalls. By the end of this lesson, you will be able to explain the fundamental principles of relational database design, including how to reduce data redundancy and improve data integrity. You'll understand the concept of normalization and its role in organizing your database tables. We'll identify and understand the goals of the first three normal forms: 1NF, 2NF, and 3NF, at a high level. Finally, you'll learn to construct SQL INNER JOIN and LEFT JOIN statements to effectively combine data from multiple tables. This foundational knowledge is key to building robust and scalable applications.
